SECRET
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 1, Special Branch
REPORT
File No. 1000
Date December 10, 1937.
Subject Hilaire du Berrier, American aviator: further report.
Made by D.S. Larby Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.I.

"Count" Hilaire du Berrier, American aviator,
who recently returned to Shanghai from Hankow by way of
Hong Kong has now removed from the Metropole Hotel to the
Cathay Mansions, Route Cardinal Mercier, where he now
occupies Room No.305.

While in Hankow, du Berrier sustained a knee
injury as a result of an aeroplane crash and thus decided
to forsake flying for the time being.

Since his return to Shanghai, du Berrier has
expressed considerable resentment at the treatment -- in a
monetary sense - - meted out to him by the Central Government
Air Force.

However he still appears to be in possession
of ample funds as may be exemplified by the fact that he
recently gave a large dinner party at the French Club; among
the guests were such well known persons as Vice Admiral Le
Bigot and Mr. M. Speelman, director of the International
Savings Society. Nevertheless, it is learned from a reliable
source that du Berrier has cabled to the Paris office of
Barclay's Bank (Dominion, Colonial and Overseas) Ltd.,
requesting the remittance of further funds. It is of
interest to observe that his mother who died in Paris about
five years ago left her son a considerable sum of money
which now forms the basis of his account with the aforementioned
bank.

If he can be taken at his word, du Berrier would
appear to be determined never again to oppose the Nationalist
forces at present taking part in the Spanish civil war.

制作人 D.S. Larby 转呈人 C. Crawford，警督。

“伯爵”希莱尔·杜·贝里埃，美国飞行员，
近期经香港从汉口返回上海，现已从麦特罗波尔酒店（Metropole Hotel）
搬至西爱咸斯路（Route Cardinal Mercier）的盖司康公寓（Cathay Mansions），
现居住于305室。

在汉口期间，杜·贝里埃因飞机坠毁导致膝盖受伤，
因此决定暂时放弃飞行。

自返回上海以来，杜·贝里埃对中央政府空军
给予他的待遇——在金钱方面——表示了相当大的不满。

然而，他似乎仍拥有充裕的资金，这可以从他最近
在法国总会举办大型晚宴这一事实中得到印证；宾客中包括
勒比戈（Le Bigot）海军中将和国际储蓄社社长斯皮尔曼（M. Speelman）先生等知名人士。
尽管如此，据可靠消息来源获悉，杜·贝里埃已致电巴克莱银行
（自治领、殖民地及海外银行）有限公司巴黎办事处，
请求汇寄更多资金。值得注意的是，其母亲约五年前在巴黎去世，
留给儿子一大笔钱，这笔钱构成了他在上述银行账户的基础。

如果信其言，杜·贝里埃似乎决心不再反对目前
参与西班牙内战的国民军部队。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, JULY 14, 1937

（印：15 JULY 1937 SHANGHAI）

Flying Soldier
Of Fortune On
Way To Spain

M. du Berrier Fails To
Sell Services In
Far East

Back to the wars again after an unsuccessful effort to sell his services to any of the Far Eastern powers, M. Hilaire du Berrier, flying soldier of fortune, sailed from Shanghai yesterday en route to war-torn Spain.

M. du Berrier, who for obvious reasons dodged publicity concerning movements, remained in Shanghai incognito for two days after an exclusive article concerning him appeared in THE CHINA PRESS last Sunday. Now the dapper young military pilot is bound for a certain European country where, according to telegraphic instructions, he is to secretly take a new war plane and deliver it to Spain.

For that he receives a bonus of £250 and on arrival in Spain will resume his job with the pursuit squadron of the Government's foreign flying force—for which he received £200 per month. Du Berrier was somewhat disappointed at his lack of success in finding a war pilot's job in the Far East and he blames it on the fact that aviation in the Orient is already too highly developed, so that there is no place for him. However, he believes that the trouble in Spain will last for at least another year, so he is sure of employment there.

Likes Excitement

Asked about the prospects of getting shot, du Berrier laughed.

"Perhaps," he said, "but anyway it's better than working. I like the excitement of it, and the comradeship of the other pilots."

The flier, who is an American of French descent, got his first taste of war in the clouds in the Italo-Ethiopian conflict. In that fray he served Haile Selassie until the rout from Addis Ababa. At the outbreak of the Spanish revolution he was among the handful of Americans, French, British and Russians who joined up with the Government forces on a cash basis. Asked which war he preferred, du Berrier said the African one, except for the fact that he was unable to collect his pay after it was over.

"All Spain has gone mad," he said, "and one is in almost as much danger from one's own allies as from the enemy. There are many opposing factions, such as the communists, anarchists and syndicalists, on the Government side and each has its own way of dealing with anyone who arouses its suspicions."

Spaniards Fighting Too

Judging by his description, almost everyone is fighting in Spain, including the Spaniards. There is little communication between different factions and the foreign fliers usually have to wait for the newspapers from France to find out what was going on.

"The airplanes we have to fly are pretty bad," he said. "Mine was a Nieuport of World War days which would only go about 80 miles an hour and turn in one direction. The Russian fliers have wonderful new machines, however, and are excellent pilots. They keep entirely to themselves, fighting their own war.

"If you lose your plane or fail to carry out orders you are shot. A friend of mine was executed because he refused to take up an old bomber which would not hold enough gasoline for him to bomb the town he had been ordered to."

Du Berrier left Spain exactly six months ago yesterday and had spent six weeks on fighting patrol in the northern part of the country. It's nearly impossible for a foreign pilot to get out of the country once he joins up, he said. He himself managed it by going on a vain errand into northern Europe in an effort to get more arms for his side. He doesn't expect to encounter any difficulty getting back in, and once there is hoping for the best.

（手写批注：el 2BR 14/7）

《字林西报》，1937年7月14日，星期三

（印：1937年7月15日 上海）

飞行雇佣兵
正前往西班牙

杜·贝里埃先生未能
在远东出售其服务

在向任何远东势力出售其服务的努力失败后，飞行雇佣兵希莱尔·杜·贝里埃先生昨日从上海启航，前往战火纷飞的西班牙。

出于显而易见的原因，杜·贝里埃先生回避了有关其行踪的宣传，在上周日《字林西报》刊登了一篇关于他的独家文章后，他在上海隐姓埋名呆了两天。现在，这位衣着考究的年轻军事飞行员正前往某个欧洲国家，根据电报指示，他将在那里秘密接收一架新式战机并将其交付给西班牙。

为此，他获得250英镑的奖金，抵达西班牙后，他将恢复在政府外籍飞行队追击中队的工作——为此他每月领取200英镑。杜·贝里埃对在远东未能找到战争飞行员工作感到有些失望，他将此归咎于东方的航空业已经过于发达，因此没有他的立足之地。然而，他认为西班牙的麻烦至少还会持续一年，所以他确信在那里能找到工作。

喜欢刺激

当被问及被击中的前景时，杜·贝里埃笑了。

“也许吧，”他说，“但无论如何总比工作好。我喜欢其中的刺激，以及其他飞行员之间的战友情谊。”

这位法裔美国飞行员在意大利-埃塞俄比亚冲突中首次尝到了空中战争的滋味。在那场混战中，他为海尔·塞拉西（Haile Selassie）效力，直到从亚的斯亚贝巴溃败。西班牙革命爆发时，他是少数几名以现金报酬为基础加入政府军的美国人、法国人、英国人和俄罗斯人之一。当被问及更喜欢哪场战争时，杜·贝里埃说是非洲那场，除了战后他无法拿到薪水这一事实外。

“整个西班牙都疯了，”他说，“一个人来自盟友的危险几乎不亚于来自敌人的危险。政府一方有许多对立派系，如共产党人、无政府主义者和工团主义者，每个派系都有自己处理任何引起其怀疑的人的方式。”

西班牙人也在战斗

从他的描述来看，几乎所有人都在西班牙战斗，包括西班牙人。不同派系之间几乎没有沟通，外国飞行员通常不得不等待来自法国的报纸来了解发生了什么。

“我们必须驾驶的飞机相当糟糕，”他说。“我的是一架第一次世界大战时期的纽波特（Nieuport）飞机，时速只能达到80英里，而且只能向一个方向转弯。然而，俄罗斯飞行员拥有奇妙的新机器，并且是优秀的飞行员。他们完全独来独往，打着自己的战争。

“如果你丢失了飞机或未能执行命令，你就会被枪决。我的一个朋友因为拒绝驾驶一架旧轰炸机而被处决，那架飞机装载的汽油不足以让他轰炸他被命令去轰炸的城镇。”

杜·贝里埃昨天正好离开西班牙六个月，并在该国北部进行了六周的战斗巡逻。他说，外国飞行员一旦加入，几乎不可能离开该国。他自己是通过前往北欧执行一项徒劳的任务，试图为其一方获取更多武器而成功脱身的。他不指望回去时会遇到任何困难，一旦到达那里，就期待最好的结果。

（手写批注：el 2BR 14/7）

possession of American passport No. 468 issued at Nice,

have stayed with friends in Shanghai for no trace of him
can be found in hotels, boarding houses or places of a
similar description in either the International Settlement
or French Concession.

According to enquiries made from various sources,
it has been ascertained that du BERRIER took part in the
Italo-Abyssinian conflict, having fought for the Negus as
a pilot of reconnaissance and bombing 'planes. With the
incidence of hostilities in Spain between the warring
factions of Loyalists and Nationalists, du BERRIER joined
up on the side of the Government forces and took part in
many air fights and skirmishes against Fascist machines.
He has been heard to remark that he was well remunerated
for his aeronautical exploits ■ in both Abyssinia and
Spain.

to Nanking and later to Kuling, in an effort to obtain a
position as an instructor ^an ■ adviser in the Chinese Air
Force, but was not successful in his quest.

Memorandum on Hilaire du BERRIER, American.

Hilaire du BERRIER alias Count du BERRIER, American
of French extraction, aged 30 or 31 years of age, in
possession of American passport No. 468 issued at
Nice, France on September 3, 1935, arrived in
Shanghai from Marseilles on May 17, 1937 by the
Messageries Maritimes' m.v. "Aramis." According
to enquiries made it has been ascertained that du
BERRIER took part in the Italo-Abyssinian conflict,
having fought for the Negus as a pilot of reconnaissance
and bombing machines. With the incidence of hostil-
ities in Spain between the warring factions of
Loyalists and Nationalists, du BERRIER joined up on
the side of the Government forces and took part in
many air fights and skirmishes against fascist
planes. He has been heard to remark that he was
well remunerated for his aeronautical exploits in
both Ethiopia and in Spain. After arrival in
Shanghai the subject made his way to Nanking and
Kuling in an effort to secure a post as an instructor
or adviser to the Chinese Air Force. He was unsuccess-
ful in his quest however.

He left Shanghai on July 13, 1937 on the s.s.
"Haruna Maru" for London, but returned here on July
31 from Hongkong on the s.s. "Niel Maersk" and again
proceeded to Nanking in search of employment in the
Chinese Air Force. He returned to Shanghai from
Hankow via Hongkong ~~in the latter part of~~ on 11 November 1937 after
sustaining a knee injury as the result of a crash.
After his return he was heard to express his resentment
vis-a-vis the financial treatment meted out to him by

关于美国人伊莱尔·杜·贝里耶（Hilaire du BERRIER）的备忘录。

伊莱尔·杜·贝里耶，又名杜·贝里耶伯爵，法裔美国人，年龄30或31岁，持有1935年9月3日在法国尼斯签发的美国护照第468号，于1937年5月17日乘坐法国邮船公司（Messageries Maritimes）的“阿拉米斯号”（m.v. "Aramis"）轮船从马赛抵达上海。据查讯获悉，杜·贝里耶曾参与意阿冲突，作为侦察机和轰炸机飞行员为尼格斯（Negus，即埃塞俄比亚皇帝）作战。随着西班牙保皇派与民族主义派敌对双方之间战事的发生，杜·贝里耶加入政府军一方，参与了许多对抗法西斯飞机的空战和小规模冲突。据闻他曾表示，他在埃塞俄比亚和西班牙的航空功绩为他带来了丰厚的报酬。抵达上海后，该对象前往南京和牯岭，试图谋求在中国空军担任教官或顾问的职位。然而他的寻求未获成功。

他于1937年7月13日乘坐“春阳丸”（s.s. "Haruna Maru"）轮船离开上海前往伦敦，但于7月31日从香港乘坐“尼尔·马士基号”（s.s. "Niel Maersk"）轮船返回此处，并再次前往南京寻求在中国空军的就业。他在汉口因坠机导致膝盖受伤后，于1937年11月11日经由香港返回上海。回来后，据闻他对中央空军给予他的财务待遇表示不满。

F. V. WAGNER and H. du BERRIER.

the object of the recent trip made to Hongkong by F. V.
Wagner and H. du Berrier was one connected with an attempt
to secure certain plans of Chinese aerodromes, airbases
and details of the location of Chinese machines. The
endeavour is said to have been successful.

the Japanese, for whom Wagner is still working as an agent.

formerly flying for the Chinese Air Force, is now acting as
an agent for the Japanese. Intelligence Service, working
in concert with Wagner.
